title: LexPilot: Benchmarking the Proactive Interaction Ability of Legal LLMs with Laypeople in Chinese Civil Case Consultation
abstract: arXiv:2610.23141v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly assisted legal professionals. However, our empirical studies reveal that, when faced with underspecified consultations from non-experts, current LLMs often produce irresponsible responses with limited utility despite lacking sufficient case details for definitive conclusions. To better assist laypeople, legal LLMs must identify focal points of dispute and proactively elicit crucial context from users. Unfortunately, existing data resources often focus on interaction and response quality, offering limited insight into how proactive interaction affects LLMs' downstream claim-level judgment prediction in actual civil cases. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{LexPilot}, a benchmark linking proactive legal interaction to claim-level verdict prediction using authentic Chinese civil judgments. translated_title: LexPilot：面向中国民事案件咨询的法律大语言模型与非专业人士主动交互能力基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已为法律专业人士提供了巨大帮助。然而，我们的实证研究表明，当面对非专业人士表述不完整的咨询时，当前的LLM即便缺乏足以得出明确结论的案件细节，也常常给出实用性有限的不负责任回复。为了更好地帮助普通民众，法律LLM必须识别争议焦点，并主动从用户处获取关键背景信息。遗憾的是，现有数据资源大多只关注交互与回复质量，对于主动交互如何影响LLM在真实民事案件中进行下游的主张层面判决预测，所提供的洞见十分有限。为填补这一空白，我们提出了LexPilot，一个利用真实中国民事判决书、将主动法律交互与主张层面判决预测相联系的基准。LexPilot基于36类常见案由的432份真实判决构建，包含专家……
tldr: 该论文提出了LexPilot基准，基于真实中国民事判决书，首次系统评测法律大模型在面对非专业人士咨询时主动追问关键案件信息并提升主张层面判决预测的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces LexPilot, a benchmark built from authentic Chinese civil judgments that systematically evaluates legal LLMs' ability to proactively elicit crucial case details from laypeople and improve claim-level verdict prediction in civil consultations.
